content.text:
Japan and Korea customers are no longer charged 100× their invoice total; `npm test` passes (9/9).

**Root cause:** `buildChargePayload` lowercases the currency for the gateway (`JPY` → `jpy`) before calling `toMinor`. The lookup in `src/lib/currency/registry.js` was case-sensitive, so `jpy` was treated as an unknown currency and fell back to the default exponent of 2. A ¥1,500 invoice became 150,000. USD and EUR were unaffected because their default exponent is already 2.

**Fix:** `exponent`, `isSupported` and `symbol` in the registry now normalize the code (trim and upper-case) before looking it up. This fixes the charge path. It also protects the other callers that pass lower-case codes, such as the ERP, CRM and tax-provider clients.

**Regression tests** (in `test/charge.test.js`):
- JPY and KRW charge payloads come out as whole units.
- `toMinor` handles lower-case `jpy` and `kwd`, which also covers the 3-decimal currencies.

I did not look at charges that were already made with the wrong amount. Any 100× charges already sent to the gateway will need refunding separately.
